title: The 10 Best Wheel Balancers
subtitle: Bubble and computerized wheel balancers for the home garage, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A wheel balancer lets you balance car and light-truck tires at home instead of paying a shop every time you swap wheels. Amazon sells two kinds: bubble balancers around $67 to $76 that find static imbalance with a level, and computerized spin balancers from about $650 to $1,200 (more when bundled with a tire changer) that also catch dynamic (side-to-side) imbalance. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (electronic readout, automatic rim measurement, alloy-wheel modes, and a stated warranty).

avoid.name: Goplus Motorcycle Wheel Balancer, Tire Balancer and Rim Wheel Balancing Stand
avoid.verdict: It shows up in Amazon's wheel balancer results at a fraction of the price of a car balancer, but it is a motorcycle stand. Car and light-truck wheels don't fit it.
reasons: The listing says it applies to motorcycle wheels: road, sport, MX and dirt bike. A car wheel has no axle hole to run a shaft through.
It balances on a horizontal shaft between two arms, which only works with spoked or narrow wheels that take an axle.
The spec table is copied from a bicycle: 5 speeds, caliper brakes and a 20 in. wheel size, none of which describe a balancer.
For a car, a $67 bubble balancer such as the MOTOOS does the job this stand can't.

buyers_guide.a: A bubble balancer (about $67 to $76) shows static imbalance: the heavy spot that makes a wheel hop. It works well for narrow car tires and occasional use. A computerized spin balancer ($650 and up) also measures dynamic imbalance, the side-to-side wobble that shows up on wide tires and at highway speed, and tells you exactly how much weight to add on each side of the rim.

The balancer can detect imbalance down to about 1 gram (0.04 oz). Wheel weights are sold in 1/4 oz (7 g) steps, so ±1 g is more precise than you can correct with standard weights. Most computerized balancers on this list claim ±1 g; a few listings give no figure.

buyers_guide.q: Will a bubble balancer fit my truck?
buyers_guide.a: The bubble balancers here fit hubs from 1-1/2 to 4 in. across, which covers most cars and light trucks. Check your wheel's center bore before buying. Heavy-duty truck wheels need a full-size machine like the KATOOL KT-B760, which takes rims up to 30 in.

ALU modes tell the balancer you're using stick-on weights on the inside of an alloy rim instead of clip-on weights on the rim edge, so it calculates weight positions for those spots. The I40 PRO, the KATOOL KT-B700 and the XK 690 list ALU modes.

Wheel weights (clip-on for steel rims, adhesive for alloys), a weight hammer or pliers, and a way to get the tire off the car. A computerized balancer also needs cones that fit your wheel's center bore; most include a basic set.
